TH.name: Thailand
TH.visa: Visa exemption up to 60 days for many passports; e-visa also available
TH.climate: Tropical — hot and humid year-round; monsoon May–Oct
TH.atmTip: ATMs widely available; foreign cards often charged ~220 THB per withdrawal
TH.transportTip: Grab is more reliable than street taxis; BTS/MRT cover Bangkok
TH.cultureTip: Remove shoes before entering temples and many homes; don't point feet at Buddha images

SG.name: Singapore
SG.climate: Tropical rainforest — hot, humid, and rainy year-round
SG.atmTip: ATMs everywhere; most foreign cards work with a small bank fee
SG.transportTip: MRT is fastest; Grab for door-to-door. Don't eat or drink on trains
SG.cultureTip: Chewing gum import is banned; littering and jaywalking are fined

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.visa: Visa exemption for many passports (typically 30–90 days)
MY.climate: Tropical — hot and humid; rain possible year-round
MY.atmTip: ATMs widely available; Maybank and CIMB usually accept foreign cards
MY.transportTip: Grab is the default; KLIA Ekspres for airport–city
MY.cultureTip: Remove shoes at mosques and some homes; dress modestly at religious sites

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.visa: e-VOA / VOA 30 days for many passports; extendable once
ID.climate: Tropical — hot and humid; wet season roughly Nov–Mar
ID.atmTip: ATMs common in cities; BCA/Mandiri work well. Daily cash limits can be low
ID.transportTip: Grab or Gojek over street taxis; Blue Bird taxis if you need a meter
ID.cultureTip: Don't touch someone's head; dress modestly at temples (sarong often provided)

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.visa: e-visa for most passports; some nationalities visa-exempt
VN.climate: Tropical — south is hot year-round; north has a cooler winter
VN.atmTip: ATMs widespread; Vietcombank and Techcombank often have lower fees
VN.transportTip: Grab is safer than hailing xe ôm; agree a price before cash taxis
VN.cultureTip: Don't point your feet at people or altars; use both hands when giving money

PH.name: Philippines
PH.visa: Visa-free 30 days for many passports; extendable on arrival
PH.climate: Tropical — hot and humid; typhoon season roughly Jun–Nov
PH.atmTip: ATMs in cities; BDO and BPI usually accept foreign cards. Rural islands: carry cash
PH.transportTip: Grab in Metro Manila and Cebu; agree jeepney/tricycle fares first
PH.cultureTip: Hospitality is serious — stay calm in public; a smile goes a long way

KH.name: Cambodia
KH.visa: e-visa or visa on arrival (typically 30 days)
KH.atmTip: USD cash is widely used; ATMs in Phnom Penh and Siem Reap. Small change often in riel
KH.transportTip: Grab in cities; tuk-tuks — agree the fare before you sit down
KH.cultureTip: Cover shoulders and knees at temples; never touch a monk

LA.name: Laos
LA.visa: e-visa or visa on arrival for many passports
LA.atmTip: ATMs mainly in Vientiane, Luang Prabang and Pakse; carry kip or Thai baht in towns
LA.transportTip: Tuk-tuks and songthaews — negotiate first; Grab is limited
LA.cultureTip: Remove shoes at temples; don't raise your voice; the head is sacred

MM.name: Myanmar
MM.visa: e-visa required for most visitors — check current advice before travel
MM.climate: Tropical monsoon — hot; rainy season roughly May–Oct
MM.atmTip: ATMs can be unreliable — carry cash USD and exchange locally
MM.transportTip: Taxis: agree the fare first; Grab may not be available
MM.cultureTip: Remove shoes at temples; don't point feet at Buddha images

BN.name: Brunei
BN.climate: Tropical rainforest — hot, humid, frequent showers
BN.atmTip: ATMs in Bandar Seri Begawan; SGD is accepted 1:1
BN.transportTip: Limited ride-hailing; airport taxis or hotel cars are easiest
BN.cultureTip: Alcohol is strictly controlled; dress modestly in public

JP.name: Japan
JP.visa: Visa exemption for many passports; eVisa for others
JP.climate: Temperate four seasons — humid summers, cold winters in the north
JP.atmTip: 7-Eleven, Japan Post and AEON ATMs are best for foreign cards
JP.transportTip: Trains first; Suica/Pasmo (or iOS Wallet) beats taxis
JP.cultureTip: Keep quiet on trains; queue; no tipping. Remove shoes indoors

KR.name: South Korea
KR.visa: K-ETA / visa-free for many passports — check before travel
KR.climate: Four seasons — humid summers, cold dry winters
KR.atmTip: Look for Global / Plus logos; convenience-store ATMs often work
KR.transportTip: T-money card + subway; Kakao T for taxis
KR.cultureTip: Remove shoes indoors; receive items with two hands

CN.name: China
CN.visa: Visa required for most; some 144-hour transit exemptions
CN.climate: Varied — humid subtropical in the south, colder and drier in the north
CN.atmTip: UnionPay ATMs; WeChat Pay / Alipay are essential for daily spend
CN.transportTip: Metro + Didi. A VPN is needed for Google, WhatsApp and many apps
CN.cultureTip: Don't stick chopsticks upright in rice; queues can be informal

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.climate: Subtropical — hot humid summers, mild winters
HK.atmTip: ATMs everywhere; HSBC and Hang Seng take most foreign cards
HK.transportTip: MTR + Octopus card; taxis are metered and plentiful
HK.cultureTip: Stand on the right of escalators; queues are taken seriously

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.climate: Subtropical — hot humid summers; typhoons Jun–Oct
TW.atmTip: ATMs widespread; 7-Eleven and post-office machines take foreign cards
TW.transportTip: MRT + EasyCard; Uber and taxis are easy in Taipei
TW.cultureTip: Remove shoes in homes; recycling rules are strict

IN.name: India
IN.visa: e-visa for many passports; apply before travel
IN.climate: Varied — tropical south, monsoon Jun–Sep, cooler north in winter
IN.atmTip: ATMs in cities; notify your bank. Keep small notes for tips and rickshaws
IN.transportTip: Uber / Ola over street taxis; metro in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru
IN.cultureTip: Right hand for eating and greeting; remove shoes at temples

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.visa: Visa-free or visa on arrival for many passports
AE.climate: Desert — very hot Apr–Oct; mild winters
AE.atmTip: ATMs everywhere; most foreign cards work with a small fee
AE.transportTip: Dubai Metro + Careem / Uber; taxis are metered
AE.cultureTip: Dress modestly; no public affection; alcohol only in licensed venues

QA.name: Qatar
QA.climate: Desert — extremely hot in summer; mild winters
QA.atmTip: ATMs common in Doha; most international cards work
QA.transportTip: Doha Metro + Karwa taxis or Uber
QA.cultureTip: Modest dress in public; Friday is the main rest day

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.visa: eVisa / visa on arrival for many passports
SA.climate: Desert — very hot summers; milder winters inland and on the coast
SA.atmTip: ATMs widely available; international cards generally work
SA.transportTip: Careem / Uber in cities; Riyadh and Jeddah metros expanding
SA.cultureTip: Alcohol is prohibited; dress modestly; Ramadan hours affect dining

AU.name: Australia
AU.visa: ETA / eVisitor required before travel for most visitors
AU.climate: Varied — temperate cities, tropical north, arid interior
AU.atmTip: ATMs everywhere; some independent machines add a fee — use bank ATMs
AU.transportTip: Opal / Myki / Go Card for city transit; Uber is widely used
AU.cultureTip: Strong sun — hat and SPF. Watch for wildlife on rural roads

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.visa: NZeTA required before travel for visa-waiver passports
NZ.climate: Temperate maritime — mild, changeable; cooler south
NZ.atmTip: Bank ATMs (ANZ, BNZ, Westpac) — avoid fee-charging independent machines
NZ.transportTip: Uber in cities; intercity buses or rental car for the rest
NZ.cultureTip: Remove shoes in many homes; respect Māori sites and don't walk on graves

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.visa: ETA required for many visa-free visitors; check before travel
GB.climate: Temperate maritime — mild, often cloudy, rain any month
GB.atmTip: Link ATMs are usually free; avoid fee-charging independent machines
GB.transportTip: Oyster / contactless on London transit; book trains ahead for lower fares
GB.cultureTip: Queueing is expected; stand on the right of escalators in London

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
NL.climate: Temperate maritime — mild, windy, frequent rain
NL.atmTip: Geldmaat ATMs; many shops are card-only — contactless is normal
NL.transportTip: OV-chipkaart / OVpay; bikes have right of way — look twice
NL.cultureTip: Be direct; don't walk in bike lanes; tap in and out on transit

FR.name: France
FR.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
FR.climate: Temperate — mild west, hotter south, colder winters in the east
FR.atmTip: Bank ATMs (BNP, Société Générale); avoid Euronet fee machines
FR.transportTip: Navigo / tickets for Métro; SNCF app for trains. 112 also works
FR.cultureTip: Always say bonjour before asking for help; keep your voice down in cafés

DE.name: Germany
DE.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
DE.climate: Temperate — warm summers, cold winters, rain any month
DE.atmTip: Sparkasse / Volksbank ATMs; many small shops are still cash-friendly
DE.transportTip: Deutschlandticket or local day tickets; validate paper tickets before boarding
DE.cultureTip: Wait for the green man; be on time; quiet hours (Ruhezeit) are real

ES.name: Spain
ES.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
ES.climate: Mediterranean — hot dry summers, mild winters; greener in the north
ES.atmTip: Use bank ATMs (Santander, BBVA, Caixa); avoid tourist-square fee machines
ES.transportTip: Metro in big cities; Renfe / Ouigo for intercity. 112 also works
ES.cultureTip: Dinner is late; greet with hola; keep an eye on bags in crowds

IT.name: Italy
IT.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
IT.climate: Mediterranean — hot summers, mild winters; Alps are alpine
IT.atmTip: Bank ATMs; avoid Euronet. Many churches require covered shoulders
IT.transportTip: Validate bus/train tickets; Trenitalia / Italo apps for long distance
IT.cultureTip: Cappuccino is a morning drink; a simple buongiorno opens every conversation

PT.name: Portugal
PT.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
PT.climate: Mediterranean — mild, sunny; wetter north, drier Algarve
PT.atmTip: Multibanco ATMs; avoid Euronet. Contactless is widely accepted
PT.transportTip: Viva Viagem / Navegante in Lisbon; Comboios de Portugal for trains
PT.cultureTip: Obrigado if you're male, obrigada if you're female; meals run long

GR.name: Greece
GR.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
GR.climate: Mediterranean — hot dry summers, mild wet winters
GR.atmTip: Bank ATMs; island independent machines can add high fees
GR.transportTip: Metro in Athens; ferries bookable on Ferryhopper. 112 also works
GR.cultureTip: A small nod upward can mean no; afternoons can be quiet for siesta

AT.name: Austria
AT.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
AT.climate: Alpine temperate — warm summers, cold snowy winters
AT.atmTip: Bankomats are widespread; Bank Austria and Erste take foreign cards
AT.transportTip: WienMobil / ÖBB; validate tickets. Sunday shops are mostly closed
AT.cultureTip: Quiet on public transport; title people (Herr/Frau) in formal settings

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
CH.climate: Alpine temperate — warm summers, cold snowy winters
CH.atmTip: PostFinance and bank ATMs; cards work almost everywhere. Euros sometimes accepted
CH.transportTip: SBB app is excellent; Swiss Travel Pass if you ride a lot
CH.cultureTip: Punctuality matters; keep your voice down on trains

BE.name: Belgium
BE.visa: Schengen visa-free for many passports (typically 90/180 days)
BE.climate: Temperate maritime — mild, grey, rain any month
BE.atmTip: Bancontact ATMs; contactless is standard. Avoid tourist-kiosk fee machines
BE.transportTip: SNCB trains + STIB/MIVB in Brussels; tap a contactless card
BE.cultureTip: Brussels is bilingual — French in Wallonia, Dutch in Flanders

US.name: United States
US.visa: ESTA (Visa Waiver) or visa required — apply before travel
US.climate: Highly varied — tropical south, arid west, four seasons in the north-east
US.atmTip: Bank ATMs (Chase, BofA, Wells Fargo); independent machines add fees
US.transportTip: Uber / Lyft in cities; transit varies — NYC subway, elsewhere often a car
US.cultureTip: Tipping 15–20% is expected in restaurants and taxis

CA.name: Canada
CA.visa: eTA for visa-exempt air arrivals; visa otherwise
CA.climate: Cold winters almost everywhere; mild wet coast in BC; hot summers inland
CA.atmTip: Big-five bank ATMs; many are surcharge-free for foreign cards besides your bank fee
CA.transportTip: Uber in most cities; Presto / Compass / OPUS for local transit
CA.cultureTip: Tipping ~15% is normal; French is expected in Québec

TR.name: Turkey
TR.visa: e-visa for many passports; some are visa-exempt
TR.climate: Mediterranean coasts, continental interior — hot summers, cold Anatolian winters
TR.atmTip: Bank ATMs (Ziraat, Garanti); avoid exchange booths in tourist squares
TR.transportTip: Istanbulkart for transit; BiTaksi or Uber. 112 also works
TR.cultureTip: Remove shoes in mosques; dress modestly; tea is hospitality
